clue.text: Sea of Tranquillity

parts.note: the lunar sea suggests the moon, but the clue wants the ocean whose name means peaceful

explanation.definitionFit: The great ocean was named by Magellan for its calm waters, and the adjective means peaceable or calm.

clue.text: Place that's next to tee in golf — this will come later

parts.note: to place something is to put it down
the letter T, spelt out as it sounds
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer's spot beside the tee, and the stroke that follows once the drive is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's next to' is a link joining the pieces. On a golf hole the tee shot comes first and the short strokes on the green come later.
explanation.definitionFit: On each hole, tapping the ball toward the cup is the final stage, after the drive from the tee.

clue.text: Unusual dialect for the kremlin?

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of the next word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An odd regional speech heard inside the Moscow seat of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A kremlin is the fortress at the heart of a Russian city, a stronghold commanding the town.

clue.text: Troubles in bars for guitarists

explanation.surface: Guitarists worrying in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be troubled is to worry, and the ridges across a guitar neck that mark the notes share the name.

clue.text: See 5 Across
Essential reading for the core curriculum?

definitions.text: Essential reading for the core curriculum?

parts.words: Essential reading for the core curriculum?
parts.note: a set text for a school syllabus, read instead as a novel whose title is about travelling down ... planet's core

explanation.surface: A recommended book for the basic school syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne's novel describes an expedition down volcanic tunnels toward the middle of our planet, the literal core.

clue.text: Sweetheart through with love's beginning to be cheerful

parts.note: jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart, as in Burns
via means by way of, through

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from the word love's

explanation.surface: Someone finished with a romance finds that a new love makes them happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. JO is the old Scots word for a darling, a common crossword stand-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial describes a jolly, good-humoured manner, a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Encourage sudden increase in power after leader's resigned

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and once it has resigned that letter is gone

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush of electric power

explanation.surface: A power spike is welcomed once the boss has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after leader's resigned' drops the first letter S from SURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to press or spur them on, a synonym of encourage.

clue.text: Vague ideas of uncharged particles?

parts.note: hazy thoughts, but read as particles without electric charge, which are 'not' the charged kind physicists name with a short word

explanation.surface: Fuzzy thinking about neutral particles in physics.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT IONS: an ion is a charged particle, so uncharged particles are not those.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions are half-formed ideas or fancies, a synonym of vague ideas.

clue.text: Tray brought round? Only if time for first of drinks — a Marine might look here

indicators.note: brought round suggests turning things about, so the letters of tray are rearranged
time is swapped for the next letter, so one letter replaces another
the first of a word is its opening letter, taken from drinks

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A waiter offers round a tray, but only when it is late enough for drinks, and a sailor watches from aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the T (time) in TRAY for D, the first of drinks, and 'brought round' rearranges DRAY into YARD. 'Only if' is a link; the clue nods to the saying that the sun is over the yardarm when drinking may start.
explanation.definitionFit: The spar across a mast was a lookout's perch, a high spot a sailor might watch from.

clue.text: See 5
Vehicle goes over large reptile and that's not all — I'm steering

indicators.note: the vehicle word turns over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

indicators.note: not all says the three letters spelling all are dropped from the reptile

parts.note: an alligator is a large reptile

explanation.surface: A driver passes over a big lizard and keeps steering on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes over' turns VAN to NAV; 'that's not all' removes ALL from ALLIGATOR, leaving IGATOR. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who plots the course and directs a ship or car is the one steering it.

clue.text: River Test commercial

parts.note: the Indus is a river of Pakistan
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A commercial on the River Test, a famous trout river in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a chalk-stream in Hampshire, England, so 'River Test' reads as one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial relates to trade and manufacturing, close in sense to commercial.

clue.text: Te-a te is a long way too short

indicators.note: cut too short means the final letter is lopped off the phrase

parts.note: so far means a long way

explanation.surface: An intimate conversation is far too brief.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned text has mangled tête-à-tête, a small two-seater couch. 'too short' drops the last letter R from SO FAR. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a small S-shaped couch seating two people side by side.

clue.text: This chap (and the taxman) will succeed

definitions.text: This chap (and the taxman) will succeed

parts.note: he means this man
IR is the Inland Revenue, the British tax authority

explanation.surface: A man and the tax office will both come into money one day.
explanation.walkthrough: IR is the Inland Revenue, the old name of the British tax office, which takes its share of an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who will succeed to a title or estate.

clue.text: Astronomer and prisoner in retreat, I stood against a pope

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the prisoner word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in old lag
Leo is the name of several popes

explanation.surface: A stargazer, once a prisoner, stood up to the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood against' is a link but fits the history: Galileo was tried by the Church and held under house arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo was the Italian scientist who turned the telescope on the planets.

clue.text: Spill the beans say and another veg

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard as spoken

parts.note: to spill the beans is to leak a secret

explanation.surface: Upsetting the beans, and then another vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' works because beans are already a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is an onion relative eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: What's no longer on board planes after midnight?

parts.note: jets are aircraft
am, ante meridiem, covers the hours just after midnight

explanation.surface: A question about what has gone from planes in the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard, so it is no longer aboard the ship.

clue.text: See 5 Across
Hunting bird from very large quarry

parts.note: OS stands for outsize
quarry is the prey being hunted

explanation.surface: A bird of prey takes a huge victim.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish-catching raptor is a bird that hunts, plunging feet first into water.

clue.text: Not Home On The Range it's not in high demand

parts.note: being off is being away, not at home or not on
a peak stands on a mountain range

explanation.surface: Someone is not keen on the cowboy song Home on the Range.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals dress it up as the cowboy song title, but they are only there for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak hours are the cheaper times when fewer people want a service.

clue.text: Where there are kings and queens partner plays highest card

definitions.text: Where there are kings and queens

parts.note: a pal is a mate or partner
to ace a trick is to play the top card

explanation.surface: At the card table a partner leads the top card among the kings and queens.
explanation.walkthrough: The kings and queens look like playing cards; they are royals.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal residences are grand houses where monarchs live.

clue.text: Heavens above, for starters order scrambled eggs

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of words, so the first letter of each of the two words is taken
scrambled eggs suggests a mix, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Good heavens, someone orders scrambled eggs as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' rearranges ORDER into RDROE after HA from 'Heavens above'.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe of a female fish is its mass of eggs.

clue.text: Where there's thatch it's frequently in bad upkeep

indicators.note: in puts the word for frequently inside the other piece
up in a down light reads a word from the bottom, so the word for bad is turned

parts.note: poor means bad
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A thatched place often falls into poor repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns POOR to ROOP, and 'in' places OFT within it. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is laid over the top of a house as its covering.

clue.text: Possibly lead me into étude's opening with a fast time

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken from étude's
into puts the word me inside the following letters

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A musician leads into a study's start with a quick tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: ME goes into E + LENT between L and N. 'lead' is the metal, not the musical lead, and 'fast' is abstaining, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead, the metal, is one example of a chemical element.

clue.text: Girl united with boy for a year

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl joins a boy for a year together.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual plant lives through one season, lasting twelve months at most.

clue.text: Double those going to church

explanation.surface: Twice as many churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold is to bend in two, and a church congregation is called a flock.

clue.text: Draw line below 19?

explanation.surface: Rule off beneath a number.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so nineteen is just below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline is to rule a stroke beneath text; and nineteen falls short of twenty, a score.

clue.text: Head of sparrow hawk is sturdy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from sparrow

parts.note: to hawk goods is to tout them

explanation.surface: A sparrowhawk's head is robust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' reads as the bird, but here it is the verb to peddle. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means strongly built, a synonym of sturdy.

clue.text: A worker's right to 26 perhaps

parts.note: a worker is a worker bee

explanation.surface: A labourer's entitlement to a stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is STOUT, a dark ale. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout is a dark kind of brewed ale.

clue.text: Without order for bank to pay, capital to remain in treasury

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
a cheque instructs a bank to pay out

indicators.note: a capital letter heads a word, so the first letter of remain is taken

explanation.surface: A capital city's funds stay in the treasury without a payment order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exchequer is the British government's finance department.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the national treasury of the UK, holding public money.

clue.text: Without reason provides shelter for eccentric

indicators.note: the two words house the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Someone irrational takes in an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional or bizarre, the same as eccentric.

clue.text: This hawk's last seen by trees flying to lake

definitions.text: This hawk's last seen by trees flying to lake

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, taken from hawk's
flying letters scatter, so trees is rearranged

parts.note: L stands for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is last spotted near woodland, flying towards a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges TREES to ESTRE. 'seen by' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This small falcon hovers over fields and roadsides, a familiar hawk in Britain.

clue.text: A dish clasping pole in nightclub

indicators.note: clasping means holding round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: hotpot is a Lancashire stew
S is south, one of the earth's poles

explanation.surface: A stew wrapped round a pole, served in a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire hotpot is a lamb and potato casserole from north-west England. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspot is a lively place of entertainment, such as a popular club.
